points.description: States that the learning rate controls the speed of convergence (of steepest descent / gradient descent towards the minimum).
States that a low learning rate gives overdamped convergence that is slow.
States that a high learning rate gives underdamped convergence that follows a zigzagging path.
Gives the danger: when the learning rate exceeds a critical value, learning becomes unstable (diverges or oscillates out of control).

rubric.notes: Full marks require all four elements stated explicitly: the learning rate controls convergence speed, low rate gives slow overdamped convergence, high rate gives underdamped zigzagging convergence, and above a critical value learning becomes unstable as the danger. Each point is all-or-nothing at harsh strictness, so vague wording such as "it can be bad if too big" or "it makes learning faster" without the stated behaviour earns nothing for that point. An error inside a point, such as calling the high-rate case overdamped or the low-rate case unstable, cancels that point.
